1.name: Point To Visual
1.desc: Starting Point: Start with creator on screen and then use finger to point to focus visual

2.name: Move In Frame
2.desc: Starting Point: Creator walks into or around the frame to give motion to the eye

3.name: Camera Whip
3.desc: Starting Point: Use fast camera whip motion to create initial stun

4.name: Jump In
4.desc: Starting Point: Creator comes into the screen from the side

5.name: Snap/Pop Reveal
5.desc: Starting Point: Use some visual signature reveal to appear in the frame

6.name: Clone // Body Double
6.desc: Starting Point: Film yourself twice. (Optional - Animate one of them.) Have both versions of you appear on the screen at the same time

7.name: Fly On Wall
7.desc: Starting Point: The subject of the video is looking off screen. Common in podcast interview style clips

8.name: Anticipated Disaster
8.desc: Starting Point: Use clip of a dangerous thing about to happen to subject in video

9.name: Object Catch
9.desc: Starting Point: Catch item thrown into frame

10.name: Using Random Product (Pope In The Pool)
10.desc: Starting Point: Use random item or task as a subconscious visual distraction

11.name: Setting Down Phone
11.desc: Starting Point: Set down recording device as video starts

12.name: Holding Prop
12.desc: Starting Point: Subject starts by holding/looking at a prop, which becomes focus of POV shot

13.name: Many Of Same Prop
13.desc: Starting Point: Multiple items. Could be similar or different

14.name: Framebreaker
14.desc: Starting Point: Remove background from initial visual and overlay it on a normal background so subject appears to break the frame

15.name: Jump Switch
15.desc: Starting Point: Creator jumps and when they land the scene changes

16.name: 3P Crash Zoom
16.desc: Starting Point: Use a shot of another person in the distance while zooming in

17.name: Fridge POV
17.desc: Starting Point: Put camera in fridge, cabinet, food aisle, etc, and then remove item/open door to reveal creator

18.name: Write On Screen
18.desc: Starting Point: Use a marker to write text on camera lens / Animate text

19.name: Mirror
19.desc: Starting Point: Creator talks to audience from reflection in mirror

20.name: Yap Cold Open
20.desc: Starting Point: Creator starts talking to audience and there is nothing happening in visual hook

21.name: A vs B Comparison Graphics
21.desc: Starting Point: Use graphics to showcase A vs B of something

22.name: Text Slide In
22.desc: Starting Point: Title text slides into video

23.name: Interactive Titles
23.desc: Starting Point: Use the title text to create motion by having it come on the screen in an interesting way

24.name: Text Arrow Pointer
24.desc: Starting Point: Use text and an arrow to direct attention at some visual while explaining what it is

25.name: Small Image Drop Overlay
25.desc: Starting Point: Use a small image to drop on a larger image and integrate the small subject into the large

26.name: Screen Recording w/ Motion
26.desc: Starting Point: Start with a screen recording using motion to aim the viewer's attention

27.name: Image Overlay Motion
27.desc: Starting Point: Use an image (with or without motion) and text to begin the video

28.name: Countdown
28.desc: Starting Point: Start the video by counting down from 3, 2, 1 before revealing something

29.name: High Motion Base B-Roll
29.desc: Starting Point: The core base visuals have high motion embedded in them

30.name: Unusual First Image/Scene
30.desc: Starting Point: Use a full screen image of something that visually breaks conventional pattern

31.name: Silent Reaction PIP
31.desc: Starting Point: Creator watches a base clip silently and then reacts

32.name: Visual Mistake
32.desc: Starting Point: Add something unexpected (that often looks like an error or glitch) to the frame

33.name: Viral Stitch Reaction
33.desc: Starting Point: Start with a viral clip and then react to it as a transition into your video

34.name: Match Cut
34.desc: Starting Point: Use a rapid series of visuals/text that line up

35.name: Visual Switch
35.desc: Starting Point: Use an action in the first shot to cleanly transition to the second shot

36.name: Beat Match Visual Switch
36.desc: Starting Point: Edit the timing of the clips turning on matched to the beat of the song

37.name: Viral Stitch Motion Match
37.desc: Starting Point: Start with a viral clip and then match cut your own motion to match

38.name: Viral Stitch Unlinked Switch
38.desc: Starting Point: Use a viral clip (high anticipation) and then cold switch to a clip of your brand/business

39.name: Speed Ramp Effect
39.desc: Starting Point: Add a speed ramp transition in the edit from shot 1 to shot 2

40.name: The Zoom In
40.desc: Starting Point: Zoom in on creator

41.name: Look Up At Camera // Top Down
41.desc: Starting Point: Film using a camera up in the corner of a room to give a different look

42.name: Sudden Danger 1P POV
42.desc: Starting Point: Use clip of a dangerous thing about to happen to viewer and fast switch/stitch

43.name: Fish Eye
43.desc: Starting Point: Film using a fish eye lens to give a different look

44.name: Frame Collapse
44.desc: Starting Point: Slowly collapse the top and bottom of the frame until it reveals an aspect ratio you want, time with beat

45.name: Crazy Transition
45.desc: Starting Point: Using high motion editing transitions or templates in Capcut

46.name: Experimental (Interactive)
46.desc: Starting Point: Use motion graphics on screen to suggest thumb movement, and then edit to match the motion

47.name: Color Switch
47.desc: Starting Point: Use any visual, start with 0 saturation, change to full color on tap/beat
